description: Deterministic qualitative contextual-risk method. level = matrix[impact][exposure]. If impact or exposure is unknown, level is unknown. Same inputs always produce the same level. Rubrics for choosing impact and exposure are normative in rfcs/0001-assessment-schema-v1.md section 5.
unknown_rule: If impact or exposure is unknown, or inputs conflict without a recorded resolution, level is unknown. Unknown is never treated, rendered, or sorted as low, and never grants permission to proceed.
compensating_control_rule: A compensating control may reduce exposure by at most one level, only with at least one current supporting evidence reference. Compensating controls never reduce impact.
downgrade_rule: Setting level below the matrix result requires a downgrade record: from_level, rationale, current supporting evidence, approver. At most one level down. Raising level above the matrix result needs no ceremony.
freshness_rule: A risk past its reassess_by, or resting on evidence past valid_until, is stale: readiness derivation treats it as unknown until reassessed.
severity_separation_rule: Contextual risk never modifies intrinsic control severity or turns a failed control into a pass; it only changes prioritisation and scoped readiness.
